title: Onboarding Access and Responsibility Contract
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the access handshake and the role-based responsibility contract used during onboarding, role changes, and offboarding. It codifies which tools get access when, the expected ownership commitments from the new hire or role-holder, and the operational SLAs for provisioning and deprovisioning.

Scope: Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and long-term vendors who require Redwood internal tool access (Okta, GCP projects, Redwood Console, Jira, Confluence, Slack, internal CI/CD, and datastore consoles). Excludes short-lived contractor access (<14 days) which is handled by the vendor liaison.

Audience: New hires, hiring managers, people-ops, IT/Identity team, security, and engineering team leads.

Quick summary
- New joiners receive a minimal viable access (MVA) within the first business day and role-complete access within the SLA below.
- Managers are accountable for confirming role responsibilities and approving elevated access.
- Access owners must attest quarterly to the necessity of each access grant.

Principles
- Principle of least privilege: grant only what is required for the role and the first 30 days of ramp.
- Transparent ownership: every access item has a named owner and purpose recorded in the access matrix.
- Time-bound escalations: elevated access must include an explicit expiration or review date.

Roles & responsibilities
- Hiring Manager: completes Role Responsibilities Form, selects template role, approves elevated privileges, and performs the first-week checklist handshake with the new hire.
- People Ops: kicks off onboarding, ensures Okta account creation, schedules badge and hardware, and tracks SLA.
- Identity/IT Team: provisions system access (Okta groups, GCP IAM, SaaS apps) and documents approvals in the provision ticket.
- Access Owner (Service/Team): validates permission set and confirms owner attestation quarterly.
- New Hire / Role-holder: signs the Responsibility Contract, completes security training, and confirms receipt and acceptance of responsibilities.

Minimum onboarding handshake (first 5 business days)
1) Day 0 (pre-boarding): People Ops opens the onboarding package with hardware, role template, and initial Okta invite.
2) Day 1 (MVA): Okta account active, Slack & Confluence access granted, corporate email provisioned, laptop assigned with disk encryption.
3) Day 2–3: Access Owner reviews role-specific groups (Jira project, Redwood Console read-only) and approves additional access via the Access Request form.
4) Day 3–5: Elevated access (write/exec) granted if approved; manager performs 'handshake' session covering responsibilities, escalation paths, and SLOs.
5) By Day 5: New hire completes security and data classification training (modules: Security Basics, Data Handling), acknowledges Responsibility Contract in Confluence.

Role handoff and backfill procedure (when someone changes roles or leaves)
1) Manager creates a Role Handoff ticket in Jira (project: PEOPLE-OPS-RUNBOOKS) with: outgoing owner, incoming owner, list of services + access level, transfer date.
2) Identity team runs an automated access diff (script: tools/identity/diff_access.sh) and lists items needing manual review.
3) Access owners must confirm within 48 hours. If confirmation not received, manager escalates to People Ops.
4) For critical production access (Console write, GCP deploy), a shadowing window of 3 business days is required where outgoing owner remains on call.
5) Completed handoffs must include an updated entry in the Access Matrix (see table below) and a signed handoff confirmation.

Access Matrix (canonical table — paste into Confluence table when executing)
- Column headings to use: Service, Typical role(s), Default level (read-only / write / admin), Provision SLA, Owner team, Required approvals, Expiration policy
- Example rows (text form):
  - Redwood Console, SRE/Platform Engineers, write, 4 business hours, Eng Platform, Manager + Identity, auto-expire 90d for temp grants
  - GCP project:redwood-prod, Release Engineers, deploy, 24 business hours, Eng Infra, Manager + Security, auto-expire 30d if tagged 'migration'
  - Jira (project:ENG), All Engineers, write, 1 business day, Engineering, Manager, persistent
  - Confluence, All employees, write by default, immediate, People Ops, Manager, persistent

Provisioning SLAs and escalation thresholds
- Standard: MVA within 1 business day; role-complete access within 5 business days.
- Urgent / Critical: critical production access (defined: deploy, secrets write, infra admin) provisioned within 4 business hours — requires Manager + Security approval by email and an automated PagerDuty alert to Identity.
- Missed SLA escalation: identity@redwood.com after the SLA window; People Ops follow-up at 24 hours; Director escalation at 72 hours.

Attestation, periodic review and deprovisioning
- Quarterly attestation: Owners receive an automated attestation email (service: AccessAudit) and must mark each account as required/optional/remove.
- Deprovisioning window: non-attested accesses flagged for removal after 14 days.
- Offboarding: on termination or exit, access is revoked automatically as follows: Okta suspend on HR termination event (t+0), GCP service accounts rotated within 24h, badges disabled t+0, laptop deprovision workflow initiated t+1.

Temporary access pattern and approval guardrails
- Temporary requests must include: business justification, time window, fallback contact, and rollback plan.
- Max temporary elevation without Exec security review: 90 days. Anything longer requires Security Director sign-off.
- Example CLI for a temporary group request (identity CLI):
  - idctl request --user alice --group infra-deploy --duration 72h --reason "critical migration" --approvers "mgr,security"

Responsibility Contract (signing checklist)
- New hire confirms: I have read the Role Responsibilities document and accept accountability for the accesses granted to me. I will:
  - Follow the Principle of Least Privilege.
  - Complete all required security training within five business days.
  - Immediately report suspected credential compromise to security@redwood.com.
  - Participate in owner attestations for services I own.
  - Keep secrets out of non-approved storage and rotate keys per policy.

Addendum: sample escalation playbook for accidental over-provisioning
1) When over-provisioning detected, file a Priority P1 Jira ticket in PEOPLE-OPS-SEC with subject: "Over-provision: <service> / <user>".
2) Identity team to suspend the offending group/permission and notify the user within 1 hour.
3) Manager must approve remediation within 8 hours or Security will require temporary suspension until review.

Tooling & automation snippets
- identity diff command (run during handoff):
  - ./tools/identity/diff_access.sh --user outgoing_user --user incoming_user --output handoff-diff.txt
- sample YAML to declare access template (stored in repo tools/identity/templates):
  - name: backend-engineer-v1
    okta_groups: ["eng-core","jira-eng"]
    gcp_roles: ["roles/viewer","roles/cloudbuild.builds.editor"]
    expiry_days: 90

Audit and metrics to track
- SLA compliance rate (weekly): target >= 98% for standard provisioning.
- Number of temporary elevations older than 30 days: target = 0.
- Quarterly attestation completion: target >= 95%.
- Monthly orphaned access (no owner): target < 2.

Ownership & escalation contacts
- People Ops (onboarding): people-ops@redwood.com
- Identity/IT: identity@redwood.com
- Security (escalation): security@redwood.com
- Directory of owners: canonical list maintained in Confluence at /confluence/access-matrix/index

How to sign off (manager checklist)
1) Confirm Role Responsibilities Form is complete and uploaded to the Jira handoff ticket.
2) Confirm hardware and credentials are delivered.
3) Conduct handshake session (cover responsibilities, incident contacts, and SLOs).
4) Mark access as accepted in the ticket and ensure the new hire has signed the Responsibility Contract in Confluence.
5) Schedule a 30-day follow-up with the new hire to verify access correctness.

Related training & resources
- Security Basics (LMS): module IDs SEC-101, DATA-102
- AccessAudit tool docs: /confluence/eng-platform/accessaudit-guide
- Okta group naming conventions: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/okta-naming

Revision history
- 2025-11-10: created by Aisha Patel (People Ops).
- 2025-12-15: added urgent access SLA and CLI examples (reviewers: Diego Morales, Emma Chen).
- 2026-02-02: clarified quarterly attestation process and deprovisioning windows.

Appendix: sample signed Responsibility Contract (to be copied into Confluence signature macro)
I, [full name], acknowledge receipt of access listed in the Jira handoff ticket [JIRA-ID], and accept responsibility for appropriate use as defined in the Redwood Responsibility Contract.\nSignature: ____________________  Date: ____/____/____

End of document.
